question: How did criterion 2 get its final form?

revisions.statement: Selectivity (real - control) at the best layer
Selectivity (real - control) at the best layer

revisions.threshold: control's max balanced accuracy over layers does not exceed the 95th percentile of 10,000 redrawn mappings
revisions.note: A leak bound, not a selectivity floor: under a type-disjoint split the control task's ceiling is chance. Drafted as 0.50 ± 0.03 (b9c861b); replaced before the push because ±0.03 fires 59–80% of the time with no leak (61bf29e).

answer:
Criterion 2 passed through three registered revisions.

- **Revision 1** (commit 12a0349, 2026-08-22): defined as selectivity, meaning real minus control, at the best layer, with a threshold of ≥ 0.10 [crit-rev1-2].
- **Revision 2** (commit c7323d0, same day): superseded revision 1. The statement stayed the same, but the threshold was marked "≥ 0.10 (provisional)" [crit-rev2-2].
- **Revision 3** (commit cb09c9d, 2026-09-26): superseded revision 2 and changed the criterion's nature. It became "Control task shows no leak." The control's maximum balanced accuracy across layers must not exceed the 95th percentile of 10,000 redrawn mappings [crit-rev3-2].

The note on revision 3 explains why. This is a leak bound, not a selectivity floor, because under a type-disjoint split the control task's ceiling is chance [crit-rev3-2]. It cites Hewitt & Liang 2019, §2.3 [paper-hewitt-liang].

The note also records an intermediate draft that was never registered. That draft used 0.50 ± 0.03 (commit b9c861b). It was replaced before the push because a ±0.03 band fires 59–80% of the time even when there is no leak (commit 61bf29e) [crit-rev3-2].

The rows do not say why the 0.10 threshold was marked provisional in revision 2.
